# Actual source normal cones and a rank-sensitive cap-cover budget

This note verifies the actual-quantile orientation, identifies the exact
face equality it forces, and records a rank-sensitive counting consequence.
Depth and cap mass throughout are UNNORMALIZED. Write
Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d, and let k(P) be the number of occupied parity classes.
No log-concavity of a projected mixed counting law is asserted.

## 1. Exact finite-buffer supporting inequality

Let Y_p=(p,y_p) be actual marks of the same deepest buffered value Q.
Let f be the actual concave buffer. Normalize the continuous part of
an actual cap N_i=(a_i,u_i) by the prescribed norm Gamma(u_i)=1.
Suppose its threshold and mass are

    c_i=N_i.Y_q-epsilon f(Y_q),     mu{N_i.w>=c_i}=Q,

and its cut is proper in the own fiber at q. Then for EVERY deepest
mark Y_p,

    N_i.Y_p-epsilon f(Y_p) <= c_i.                    (1)

Indeed, if the displayed buffered threshold at p exceeded c_i, the
parallel cap through that buffered threshold would lose a positive
own-q slab from the actual cap. Its mass would be strictly below Q,
contradicting the buffered depth at Y_p. The strict slab exists at c_i
because the own-q cut is proper; monotonicity then treats any larger
threshold. This proves the orientation without a centroid argument.

Suppose positive weights rho_i sum to one and the actual contact equation
is sum rho_i u_i=epsilon g. Suppose (alpha,g) is a FULL supergradient of
f at Y_q, as proved for the selected buffer in
`candidate 9158d8d941246660`.
Put

    a=sum rho_i a_i-epsilon alpha,    B=conv{p: Y_p is deepest}.

Summing (1) and using the supergradient inequality gives

    a.(p-q)<=0  for every deepest base p.             (2)

Thus a belongs to the OUTWARD normal cone N_B(q), relative to aff B.
The epsilon alpha correction is essential; sum rho_i a_i alone need
not support B at positive epsilon.

Let F be the minimal face of B containing q. Every outward support
functional at q is constant on F. For p in F, the weighted left slack
in (1) equals

    a.(p-q)+epsilon[alpha.(p-q)+g.(y_p-y_q)
                                      -(f(Y_p)-f(Y_q))].

The first term is zero, the bracket is nonnegative, while each
individual quantile slack is nonpositive. Hence the weighted sum and
ALL its positively weighted summands vanish. At epsilon>0 the bracket
also vanishes. Consequently all these ACTUAL cap quantiles are equalities
at every deepest mark whose base is in F. This is the precise face
rigidity behind the normal-cone description.

## 2. The genuine unbuffered statement and its limit scope

At epsilon=0, the same proof applies directly to actual deepest marks
and actual proper mass-Q caps. Given a positive continuous-normal balance

    sum lambda_i u_i=0,   sum lambda_i=1,

put a=sum lambda_i a_i. Then a is in N_B(q), and every selected cap plane
contains every deepest mark over the minimal face F of q.

If q is in relint B, a annihilates lin(B-B). This is full-space balance
ONLY relative to that base span; perpendicular base components may survive.
If B has full base dimension, a=0 in the full base space.

When the marked graph over F is affine, y_p=A p+b, the common cap equations
imply a_i+A^T u_i annihilates lin(F-F), individually. Thus after the
actual fiber shear x'=x-Az-b, all cap base coefficients vanish on this
span. If F has full base dimension, the caps are exactly cylindrical
halfspaces u_i.x'>=0. A selected minimal circuit of continuous rank r then
has full ambient normal rank r as well.

A limit of finite-buffer certificates may use these conclusions only
after checking vanishing buffer thresholds, convergence of the relevant
normal coefficients, nonzero limiting continuous normals, and the retained
cap-mass upper bounds. Finite-buffer balance is sum rho_i u_i=epsilon g,
not zero. No arbitrary interchange of limit and closed cap mass, or of
finite-buffer contacts and unbuffered centers, is licensed here.

## 3. A direct quota for target fibers, including non-source fibers

This statement needs no concavity hypothesis or optimality beyond its
actual cap budgets. Suppose r+1 actual caps H_i all contain a common
point Y_q on their boundaries, their continuous normals form a minimal
positive circuit of rank r, and mu(H_i)<=Q. Write their margins as

    a_i.(z-q)+u_i.(x-y_q),

and let a=sum lambda_i a_i for the positive balancing weights. Then

    sum lambda_i margin_i(z,x)=a.(z-q).               (3)

Therefore these CLOSED caps cover the ENTIRE continuous fiber plane at
every base z with a.(z-q)>=0. If E is any set of actual base indices on
that side, writing M_E=sum_(z in E)|K_z| gives the exact bound

    M_E <= sum_i mu_E(H_i) <= (r+1)Q.                 (4)

All overlaps remain in the first sum; none is discarded or counted with
a negative weight. In particular, when a annihilates aff(B)-q,

    Q >= M_(P intersect aff(B))/(r+1).                (5)

This includes target fibers outside the source face but in its affine
span. In the full-base-dimensional case it gives Q>=M/(r+1).
This is stronger in its target range than the source-face-only quota,
but its numerical factor is merely the cap count.

For s groups whose covered base sides jointly cover P, with continuous
ranks r_1,...,r_s and a common individual cap budget Q, (4) gives

    M <= Q sum_(j=1)^s (r_j+1).                        (6)

Thus this actual certificate alone establishes the proposed OC bound
Q>=Gamma_d M/k(P) whenever

    sum_j(r_j+1) <= k(P)/Gamma_d.                      (7)

In particular, if s<=k(P) and every selected group has rank one, (7)
holds in every d>=1 because Gamma_d<=1/2. For one full-base source group,
(7) holds whenever k(P)>=(r+1)Gamma_d; if k(P)>=2, ranks r<=3 always
satisfy this, using r<=d and Gamma_d<=Gamma_r.

For general k(P), the number-of-groups input must actually have been
proved with that parity count. Replacing 2^n by k(P) without its finite
witness/parity argument is not implicit in (6). The finite certificate in
`candidate d2b290ebd8e35052` provides such an argument when
its witnesses lie in P. Its auxiliary real contacts are not thereby
identified with actual deepest source marks.

## 4. An exact actual-critical calibration, including all cap budgets

Take n=d=1 and C=[0,1] times [-1,1]. There are exactly two integer fibers,
M=4, and k(P)=2. The points Y_0=(0,0),Y_1=(1,0) have depth Q=1:
every containing cap contains at least a half interval in its own fiber,
while a sufficiently large base tilt isolates that half interval.
At any other point the smaller isolated interval half gives depth at most
one, so Q is the exact GLOBAL maximum.

Use the two groups

    z=0:  x-2z>=0,       -x-2z>=0;
    z=1:  x+2(z-1)>=0,   -x+2(z-1)>=0.

Every cap has mass EXACTLY one and is proper in its own source fiber.
Every group has continuous rank one and weights (1/2,1/2).
Their summed base normals are -2 and +2, respectively, exactly the
outward directions at the endpoints of B=[0,1]. The other source mark
has strict negative margin in each cap. The two covered base sides are
z<=0 and z>=1 and cover P. Equality holds in (6): M=4Q.
Thus the rank-one count is calibrated by actual common-critical caps at
actual global maxima, not by arbitrary cap allocations. Boundary normal
cones do not give a spurious full-space balance.

## 5. What is already archived, and what remains blocked

The integer-tilt zonotope inclusion and the stronger orientation-resolved
outside-facet payment were checked against the registry and already occur
in `candidate 090886b0cc1f399f` and
`candidate e81d0f726880ea4a`. They are dependencies,
not new progress here. In particular every common equality cap has the
exact proper-section plus full-support penalty paid by empty-support
facets outside a two-source slab. Those conditions do not themselves
supply a new Gamma payment.

Even in the full-base-dimensional sheared setting the actual projected
law is f(x)=sum_z 1_(K_z-y(z))(x). The affine homothetic source core and
its global containing homotheties do not, by themselves, turn this sum
into a projected uniform convex law. The archived roof counterexamples
exclude that claim without the actual common-critical-source hypothesis;
they are NOT counterexamples retaining that extra hypothesis.

No exact counterexample with all of the narrowed full-dimensional
source-face/actual-critical conditions has been produced here, and no
higher-rank Gamma improvement is proved. Beyond (7), turning the normal
cone geometry into a shared concave cap law still has the same missing
mass-payment bridge. The normal-cone orientation, face equalities, and
rank-sensitive cover quota above are valid; a general projected-law
concavity or Gamma conclusion would be an unsupported extra assumption.
